_about: Every number here is an ASSUMPTION made for the Phase 1 model, not a rule from the Rules of Play. Each has a unit and a reason. Change them here; nothing in the engine hard-codes these values. Run analyses at more than one setting before trusting a conclusion.

tick_seconds.why: Resolution of the round-based loop. Melee exchanges and incantation progress are resolved once per tick.

speech_words_per_second.why: Incantation time = words x repetitions / this rate. 3.5 words/s is about 210 words a minute: a practiced player reciting a memorized, repeated incantation, still audible at 20' with no two-second gaps. Was 2.5 (150 wpm, ordinary conversation), which made a Heal 16 s and a Magic Ball 10 s and left 6th-level players barely better than 1st-level ones (face-validity check 'level': 0.555 at 2.5, 0.683 at 3.5, 0.733 at 4.5 words/s).

charge_incantation_words.why: Counted from the Charge Incantation in rules/magic-states-effects/mechanics-and-definitions.md. Listed here so charge time uses the same speech rate.

sd.why: Player fighting skill is drawn from Normal(0, sd). Scenarios can widen or narrow the spread.

logit_per_sd.why: How strongly a one-sd skill gap moves the chance of landing a hit.

base_hit_per_second.why: Chance an attacker lands a valid hit on one engaged opponent in one second, equal skill, no shield.

shield_logit.why: Larger shields make the bearer harder to hit.

gang_logit_per_extra_attacker.why: Each extra attacker on the same defender makes each attacker more likely to land a hit.

wounded_leg_logit.why: A kneeling or posting player is easier to hit.

wounded_weapon_arm_logit.why: Attacking with the off hand after the weapon arm is wounded.

no_weapon_attack_scale.why: A player whose melee weapon is destroyed cannot attack until it is repaired (no backup weapon modeled).

hit_location_weights.why: Where landed melee and projectile hits strike.

great_weapon_share.why: Share of shield-less players of classes allowed All Melee who use a two-handed Great weapon (Armor Breaking + Shield Crushing per rules/weapon-types-shields-equipment.md).

shield_use_share.why: Share of players allowed a shield who carry one (their largest allowed size).

stunned_logit.why: A Stunned player cannot defend, so hits on them land far more often.

weak_weapon_logit.why: Magic Users and Archers fighting with a dagger, staff or short weapon.

p_shield_struck_on_miss.why: When an attack with Shield Crushing misses a shield bearer, this often it struck the shield instead (three hits destroy it).

p_engage_per_second.why: Chance a free melee player reaches an enemy in one second (non-spatial stand-in for movement).

backline_factor.why: Casters and archers stay back, so enemies reach them at this fraction of the normal rate.

p_disengage_per_second.why: Chance an engaged pair breaks apart in a second without a death.

caster_weight_when_choosing_melee_target.why: Fighters slightly prefer to go after reachable casters.

p_in_range.why: Chance the intended target is within the ability's range when the caster wants to cast. Checked when the incantation starts.

p_ally_nearby_for_touch.why: Chance a chosen friendly target is close enough for Touch or Other.

p_interrupt_on_armor_hit.why: A caster struck on armor while incanting moves their feet or loses the incantation this often. Wounds, death and action-preventing states always interrupt (rules: feet may not move; Magic Users need an empty hand).

engaged_casting_allowed.why: Policies do not start non-Self incantations while engaged in melee.

magic_ball_p_hit.why: Chance a thrown Magic Ball strikes its target.

magic_ball_retrieve_seconds.why: Time to pick thrown balls back up once none are in hand.

arrow_p_hit.why: Chance an arrow strikes its target.

arrow_shot_seconds.why: Nock, draw and aim time per shot. Arrows are Armor Breaking (rules/weapon-types-shields-equipment.md).

thrown_p_hit.why: Chance a thrown weapon (javelin, rock) strikes. Not yet used by Phase 1 policies.

rejoin_seconds.why: Time from respawning at base to rejoining the fight. Enchantments can be cast during this time.

pregame_prep_seconds.why: Time at the start of a game when players at base cast enchantments before fighting.

look_the_part_share.why: Share of players awarded Look The Part.

archetype_share.why: Share of 6th-level players who take an optional Archetype (chosen uniformly among options).

magic_user_copy_cap.why: Magic Users buy at most this many copies of a spell whose Max is not listed.

armor_worn_share.why: Share of players allowed armor who wear their class maximum on every location (the rest wear none).

revive_priority.why: Support casters try to return dead allies to life before anything else.

p_use_offensive_ability_when_free.why: Chance a free martial player with a usable offensive ability casts it instead of closing to melee.

self_insubstantial_seconds.why: How long a player stays in a self-imposed Insubstantial state (Blink etc.) before returning.

forced_move_seconds.why: How long Shove/Push/keep-away style effects keep a player out of melee when the rule gives no duration.

p_charge_when_safe.why: Chance an unengaged player with a spent chargeable ability starts the Charge incantation.

p_enchant_ally_on_field.why: Chance a free enchanter tries to enchant an unenchanted ally on the field (rather than only at base).

abandon_cast_when_attacked.why: A player attacked in melee mid-incantation or mid-Charge stops and defends unless the incantation completes this second. Standing still and talking while being hit is how a veteran caster gets killed; they break off and fight or back away.

max_seconds.why: Hard time cap. Games at the cap are scored by remaining lives or kills.

level_weights.why: Placeholder level mix until ORK attendance data is available.

class_weights.why: Placeholder: uniform class mix until ORK data is available.
